title: Microsoft shares how to fix broken Exchange Online EWS apps
description: Microsoft is retiring the Exchange Web Services (EWS) API in Exchange Online, which causes EWS-dependent applications to stop working when the API is disabled. IT administrators can temporarily re-enable EWS to restore functionality until the final shutdown on April 1, 2027. Microsoft recommends updating or replacing applications to use the Microsoft Graph API, which offers similar features. The retirement affects only Exchange Online and Microsoft 365 environments; on-premises Exchange Server installations remain unaffected.
aiSummary: Microsoft announced the phased retirement of the Exchange Web Services (EWS) API in Exchange Online, starting with blocking EWS by default on October 1, 2026, and final shutdown on April 1, 2027. EWS is used by various applications to access mailbox items in Exchange Online. When disabled, these apps encounter errors or repeated authentication prompts. Administrators can temporarily re-enable EWS via the Microsoft 365 admin center or Exchange Online PowerShell commands to restore app functionality. Microsoft advises developers to migrate to the Microsoft Graph API, which provides near-complete feature parity. The retirement applies only to Exchange Online and Microsoft 365; on-premises Exchange Server continues to support EWS.
aiImpact: Applications relying on the EWS API in Exchange Online will fail to function properly once EWS is disabled, resulting in errors and authentication prompts. This disrupts user access to mailbox data through affected apps such as older Outlook versions, Apple Mail/Calendar on macOS, and other third-party applications. The disruption impacts tenant administrators and end users until apps are updated or EWS is re-enabled temporarily. There is no indication of a security vulnerability or exploit; the impact is operational due to API deprecation.
